questions.q: Why is a manual journal described as its own origin, unlike most subledger-sourced journals?
options: Because manual journals never post to General Ledger
Because a person typed it directly, rather than it being generated from an upstream business transaction
Because manual journals cannot be drilled into at all
Because manual journals always involve foreign currency
questions.explain: A manual journal is entered directly by a person, so there is no further upstream transaction to drill into — it is the origin itself.

questions.q: What is the role of Subledger Accounting (SLA) in the drill path?
options: It deletes subledger transactions after they post
It replaces the need for a chart of accounts
It only applies to manual journals
It generates the debits and credits from a subledger transaction that ultimately post to General Ledger as a journal
questions.explain: SLA is the engine that converts subledger transactions into accounting entries, which then post to GL — making the GL journal often a summary of that activity.

questions.q: Put the drill path in the correct order, from where an inquiry starts to the final stop.
options: Subledger transaction, journal lines, account balance, subledger journal entry
Journal lines, subledger transaction, account balance, subledger journal entry
Account balance, journal lines, subledger journal entry, subledger transaction
Subledger journal entry, account balance, subledger transaction, journal lines
questions.explain: The correct path starts at a summarized balance, drills to journal lines, then to the subledger journal entry, and finally to the originating subledger transaction.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation example, what does drilling on an unusual Accounts Payable liability balance eventually reveal?
options: A random account combination with no further detail
Only the budget for Accounts Payable
The chart of accounts structure for the ledger
A specific supplier invoice, reached through journal lines and the subledger journal entry
questions.explain: The drill path ends at the subledger transaction, which in this case is the specific supplier invoice that actually explains the balance.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe the drill path as a bridge into the next course?
options: Because this course covered the GL side — starting from a balance and walking backward — while the subledger course shows the same chain from the transaction forward
Because the next course has nothing to do with General Ledger
Because Accounts Payable does not use Subledger Accounting
Because drilling down is only relevant during year-end close
questions.explain: This course teaches walking backward from a GL balance; the Accounts Payable course picks up the same chain from the transaction side, showing how it becomes a journal in the first place.
